subject: Edge OTLP relay sandbox onramp — pilot plan and next steps
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@datadog.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: María Gómez <maria@grafana.com>, EdgeOps Consulting <edgeops@integral.consulting>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Edge OTLP relay pilot — quick kickoff proposal

Hi Sofia / Ben,

Thanks again for the intro. We chatted with María and the EdgeOps team this morning — there’s strong mutual interest in validating a lightweight OTLP relay that can run in customer edge clusters and fan out telemetry to Datadog and Grafana Cloud without touching customer PII. High level ask: run a 6-week sandbox with Example Corp to validate throughput, cert rotation, and relay routing rules.

Key constraints we heard from the customer:
- No persistent logs in the relay VM; only transient buffering (under 30s)
- TLS mutual auth to Datadog and Grafana endpoints
- Per-tenant routing config that can be changed via a management API

Can Redwood provide:
1) a slimmed container image + CPU/GPU footprint guidance for edge sizing
2) a SAML-friendly onboarding flow or temporary token approach for the sandbox
3) a brief mutual action plan and success criteria we can share with procurement

I attached a short architecture sketch for discussion (edge-otlp-relay-arch.pdf). Would love to kick off a 30m sync next week to align SLOs and schedule.

Samir
Solutions Engineer, Datadog

Attachments: edge-otlp-relay-arch.pdf
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@datadog.com>, María Gómez <maria@grafana.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, EdgeOps Consulting <edgeops@integral.consulting>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edge OTLP relay pilot — quick kickoff proposal

Thanks Samir — this looks actionable. Copying Laura and Ben to own the commercial and technical coordination respectively. A few immediate clarifications from our side:

- We can provide a minimal container image (no GPU) and a sizing table for common edge classes (t3.medium, c5.large equivalent).
- For the sandbox we recommend short-lived tokens (rotated daily) backed by a Redwood-managed key in the control plane; we can map that to a SAML assertion for customers that want SSO.
- We prefer to keep buffering at the relay ephemeral (in-memory) and rely on the management API to throttle.

Next steps we propose:
1) Ben to produce a short implementation checklist (certs, ports, TLS ciphers)
2) Laura to draft a mutual action plan and a one-page commercial note for procurement
3) 30m sync with Example Corp + EdgeOps on Wednesday 12/16 at 11am PT — please confirm availability

Sofia
Director, Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Edge OTLP relay pilot — quick kickoff proposal

Quick tech note ahead of the sync:

- Certs / mTLS: We should standardize on a short rotation window (24h tokens + 7d certs) to keep key compromise blast radius small. Karthik, can you shepherd a short doc for cert rotation? I attached cert-rotation-notes.md for discussion.
- Ports: relay will need outbound 443 to Datadog and Grafana endpoints, plus 8443 for the management API if we host it behind the relay.
- Resource profile: for the initial sandbox we suggest 1 vCPU + 1GB RAM per 10k rps (in practice we expect <2k rps). We'll provide a microbenchmark.
- Observability: Redwood will emit internal metrics (relay.health, relay.buffer_ms, downstream.success.rate) to a staging Datadog account so we can validate telemetry fidelity end-to-end.

I will ship the checklist and microbenchmark before the Wednesday sync.

Ben
Principal Engineer, Integrations — Redwood Inference

Attachments: cert-rotation-notes.md

Subject: Re: Edge OTLP relay pilot — quick kickoff proposal

Thanks all — this aligns with Grafana Cloud requirements. A few items from our side:

- We'll provide a scoped API key for the sandbox (read/write only for metrics/traces) and an ingestion endpoint that supports OTLP over gRPC.
- We recommend adding a lightweight config flag to enable/disarm header stripping so customer headers with PII are dropped at the relay.
- We'll join the Wednesday sync and can demo an ingestion test with a small script.

Also attaching a short mutual action plan CSV that our PM used in a prior pilot — adapt as you like.

María
Partner PM, Grafana Labs

Attachments: mutual-action-plan.csv
